questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Papua New Guinea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Papua New Guinea article.

questions.proof: The capital city of Papua New Guinea is Port Moresby.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Papua New Guinea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Papua New Guinea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Papua New Guinea article.

questions.proof: It borders Indonesia to the west and near Australia to the south.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Parliament has approved two additional provinces by _____: Hela Province, which will be part of the current Southern Highlands Province, and Jiwaka Province, which will be formed by dividing Western Highlands Province.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Papua New Guinea article, under the heading “Administrative divisions”.

questions.proof: Parliament has approved two additional provinces by 2012: Hela Province, which will be part of the current Southern Highlands Province, and Jiwaka Province, which will be formed by dividing Western Highlands Province.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “A study in _____ found that it was about 50,000 years ago that these people came to a big land called Sahul, which is Australia and New Guinea combined.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Papua New Guinea article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: A study in 2016 found that it was about 50,000 years ago that these people came to a big land called Sahul, which is Australia and New Guinea combined.
